root_cause: Console.is_terminal had no way to override TTY detection from the environment except FORCE_COLOR (any value, even '' or '0', forced True). The maintainer's spec for the new TTY_COMPATIBLE variable exists only in a comment on issue #2924: '1' = assume a TTY, '0' = assume not a TTY, blank or anything else = auto-detect via file.isatty().
best_solution: In rich/console.py Console.is_terminal, after the explicit force_terminal check and the idle/Jupyter checks, read `tty_compatible = environ.get('TTY_COMPATIBLE', '')`; if == '0' return False; if == '1' return True; otherwise fall through. Then FORCE_COLOR: `if force_color is not None: return force_color != ''` (no longer caching into self._force_terminal), then the existing isatty() auto-detect. Gold also made NO_COLOR ignore an empty value (`environ.get('NO_COLOR','') != ''`) and added TTY_COMPATIBLE to the env list in rich/diagnose.py (neither is tested). Reasoning: a *_COMPATIBLE flag is a boolean override, so it needs three states (force on, force off, defer to detection), and it must short-circuit before isatty is called.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_console.py::test_tty_compatible using FakeFile/FakeTTY objects whose isatty() records called_isatty. Cases (env passed via Console(_environ=...)): no env + non-TTY -> is_terminal False, isatty called; TTY_COMPATIBLE='1' + non-TTY -> True, isatty NOT called; FakeTTY + no env -> True, called; TTY_COMPATIBLE='' -> True, called (auto-detect); 'whatever' -> True, called; TTY_COMPATIBLE='0' + FakeTTY -> False, isatty NOT called. The rest of the diff only adds '-> None' annotations. The old parametrized test_force_color(['', 'something', '0']) is shadowed by a later function with the same name, so FORCE_COLOR='' semantics go untested.
locating_signals: The title and body name only the env var `TTY_COMPATIBLE` plus a link to issue #2924, with no semantics. Grepping for FORCE_COLOR / isatty / _environ leads to Console.is_terminal in rich/console.py, and the function is not named. The value semantics are in a maintainer comment on #2924 that the agent cannot see.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8) FAIL in the Kaggle env with the same error: test_tty_compatible fails at the TTY_COMPATIBLE='' case (`assert console.file.called_isatty`, line 1098); 98 other tests pass. Every patch copied the existing FORCE_COLOR idiom 'any value at all means terminal'. v4 added `if self._environ.get('TTY_COMPATIBLE') is not None: return True` after the FORCE_COLOR block. v6/v7/v8 (identical) OR-ed it into the FORCE_COLOR condition and also cached `self._force_terminal = True`. So '' and 'whatever' skip auto-detect, and '0' returns True where it should return False. Right location, wrong semantics: none implemented the 0/1/else tri-state.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement adds a boolean-like env var or config flag without saying what its values mean, do not copy a neighbouring 'present means true' idiom. Implement the conventional tri-state: '1' forces on, '0' forces off, and empty, unset or any other value falls back to the existing auto-detection, which must then actually run. Put the check before the expensive or auto-detect path so a forced value short-circuits it, and don't cache the result into a field that disables later detection. Keep explicit constructor arguments above the env var. If the statement is only a title plus an issue link, assume the real spec is in that discussion, and write a quick check that '0' disables and '' defers.
acceptable_alternatives: Any is_terminal ordering works if TTY_COMPATIBLE is checked before isatty: exactly '0' -> False and exactly '1' -> True without calling isatty, and every other value (including '') falls through to auto-detect. Where it sits relative to FORCE_COLOR is untested. The NO_COLOR and diagnose.py changes are optional.
